Subject: CascadeBank: network isolation & egress controls — RFP questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. CascadeBank's security team is compiling answers for our vendor RFP and we have a few clarifications before we slot Redwood into our third-party review. Could you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Control-plane vs data-plane separation: does Redwood run any customer-specific control-plane components in shared subnets or does each account get isolation at the control-plane layer?
2) Egress filtering: do you provide per-tenant egress allowlists or is egress enforced at the cluster/broker level only?
3) Sidecar/agent egress: are model sidecars allowed to make arbitrary outbound connections, or are egress flows mediated by a tenant-specific proxy?
4) Threat model summary: can you provide a concise (1–2 page) summary of the primary attack paths you consider for multi-tenant inference (especially lateral movement via shared KV/cache and sidecar-to-control-plane channels)?

We'd prefer a succinct PDF and any diagrams. Also let us know if any items require an NDA or if we should submit a formal evidence packet.

Regards,
Emily Turner
Senior InfoSec Manager, CascadeBank
security@cascadebank.com

Attached are the artifacts we commonly provide for these RFPs (redacted):
- cascadebank_vpc_diagram_v1.png (diagram showing tenant VPCs, control-plane endpoints in a customer-specific VPC or private link model, and sidecar placement within tenant compute pools)
- egress_matrix_v2.csv (matrix mapping egress destinations to enforcement layer: sidecar, tenant-proxy, cluster-egress)

Short answers to Emily's bullets (for the summary):
1) Control-plane isolation: we operate a customer-dedicated control-plane instance for Dedicated and Private customers. Hosted customers may share global control-plane services behind strict tenant authentication; in those cases, customer metadata and auth tokens are strongly compartmentalized, and we provide private-link/VPC peering options for enhanced separation.

2) Egress filtering: we support per-tenant egress allowlists for Dedicated and Private deployments. In Hosted, egress is enforced at the service boundary by tenant-scoped proxies and at the platform edge; we can push tenant-specific ACLs when requested under enterprise contracts.

3) Sidecar egress: model-sidecars default to a restricted mode — outbound is mediated via a tenant proxy or sidecar-controlled policy. Unrestricted outbound is not permitted for tenants by default; any exceptions require explicit approval and a compensating control (mTLS + static egress ACL).

4) Threat model summary (bullets for the 1–2 page PDF):
- Attack vector: shared KV/cache theft — mitigations: per-tenant cache keys, tenant-scoped encryption, strict ACLs on KV reads/writes, and periodic cache key rotation.
- Attack vector: lateral movement from a compromised sidecar — mitigations: sidecar sandboxing, no-disk policy, eBPF-level syscall filtering, and tenant proxy egress validation.
- Attack vector: control-plane compromise — mitigations: customer-dedicated control-plane for Dedicated/Private, RBAC, audit logging to tamper-evident store, and multi-region recovery for availability.

Send to Emily with a short 1–2 page brief and include the annotated diagram. I attached the two files above (redacted copies).

Attached: redwood_threat_summary_20270625.pdf (1.5 pages, executive bullets + mitigations), cascadebank_vpc_diagram_v1.png, egress_matrix_v2.csv. Quick answers below so your RFP team can copy/paste: 

Telemetry & audit exports (Hosted):
- Audit logging: request-level logs retained by default for 90 days; longer retention is available as an enterprise add-on (custom retention to S3 or log storage).
- SIEM integration: we can forward structured audit events (JSON) to customer-managed endpoints via secure push (TLS + mutual auth) or deliver via S3 push.
- Token-level tracing: we can provide per-request IDs and tokenization metadata; full prompt text export requires customer consent and is gated by contract and data residency settings.

Sidecar egress enforcement:
- Enforcement model: application-level proxying combined with network ACLs. Sidecars are configured to route outbound traffic through a tenant proxy that enforces allowlists; at the infra level, cluster egress gateways provide defense-in-depth.

NDA note: the PDF and diagram are redacted for public review. If CascadeBank would like non-redacted logs or raw telemetry, please share your standard NDA and we'll coordinate with Legal.

Next steps: Ben will open a HubSpot support ticket with the full evidence packet and I'll include the Drive link. If you want a short call to walk through the diagram and threat bullets, Markus is available Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks — hope this helps the RFP submission.
